Its optimality system takes the form of a McKean-Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE), in which the marginal terms act continuously in time while the path-law term instead induces conditional adjoint jumps at the observation dates. We derive the reduced FBSDE for quadratic control cost and constant diffusion, establish local well-posedness for a Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) path-law formulation, and develop a sample-based neural solver with causal representations. Experiments on synthetic transport, latent face transport, and human motion validate the framework. In particular, a two-state AMASS experiment under path-law supervision captures both low-to-high and high-to-low transitions, which marginal supervision alone cannot distinguish.
item.dc:creator: Samer El Boustany, Samy Mekkaoui, Yadh Hafsi, Alexandre Alouadi, Huy\^en Pham

item.title: Service-Induced Congestion in Memory-Constrained LLM Serving
item.description: arXiv:2606.15555v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In large language model (LLM) serving, each request accumulates persistent graphics processing unit (GPU) memory during service as its key-value cache grows with every generated token. Under high concurrency, aggregate memory usage therefore increases endogenously over time: the service process itself creates future capacity pressure. When memory capacity is exceeded, systems evict active requests, discarding cached state and restarting them later, which wastes computation and reduces throughput. We develop a discrete-time dynamical model of memory-constrained LLM inference that captures admission, memory growth, and eviction under continuous batching. In the saturated-input regime, the system admits both eviction-free fixed points and limit cycles with evictions. For homogeneous workloads, we show that the eviction-free equilibrium is unstable and that, except for a Lebesgue-measure-zero exact-capture set, the system converges to a unique worst-case limit cycle that is asymptotically stable outside this exceptional set, with throughput losses as large as 50%. For heterogeneous workloads, we prove a stability criterion in the two-class common-input setting and explain how the survival-polynomial mechanism generalizes to multiple classes and heterogeneous-input lengths. Under an input-dominated scaling regime, coprime decoding lengths stabilize the eviction-free equilibrium, while non-coprime lengths create synchronized modes that drive instability. These results characterize when workload heterogeneity desynchronizes completions and helps stabilize memory-constrained serving. More broadly, we identify service-induced congestion as a structural instability mechanism and derive scheduling design principles for sustaining high throughput.
item.dc:creator: Ruicheng Ao, Jing Dong, Gan Luo, David Simchi-Levi

item.title: PhiBE-Q-Learning: Bridging Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning and Continuous-Time Control
item.description: arXiv:2606.21925v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop an off-policy method for continuous-time reinforcement learning (CTRL), where the system dynamics are governed by an unknown stochastic differential equation (SDE) and only discrete-time trajectory data are available. A central challenge is that the classical discrete-time state--action value function loses its action-dependent signal in the continuous-time limit (Baird, 1994; Jia and Zhou, 2023; Tallec et al., 2019). On the other hand, continuous-time control provides local notions such as the instantaneous advantage function $q(s,a)$, but these typically rely on state value function $V(s)$. To obtain a formulation with a single unknown function, we introduce a new definition of the state--action value function $Q(s,a)$ in CTRL and derive its governing equation. Building on the PhiBE approximation (Zhu, 2024; Zhu et al., 2025), we propose iterative algorithms to approximate the optimal $Q$-function in both model-based and model-free settings using only discrete-time off-policy data. Under linear function approximation, we establish error bounds and explicit convergence rates for the algorithm in the popoluation level. The finite-data algorithm is evaluated numerically.
item.dc:creator: Yuhua Zhu

item.title: Optimal Selling of Defaultable Assets using the Distribution Builder
item.description: arXiv:2608.21716v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the problem of when it is best to sell a risky asset in the \textit{distribution builder} framework under the consideration of potential ruin. This approach allows investors to express their preferences directly as a desired target distribution without first specifying a risk aversion or utility function. Mathematically, the problem is closely related to the Skorokhod embedding problem of attaining a given distribution by stopping a diffusion process. We work in a general framework of one-dimensional diffusion processes and extend existing results to include the possibility of ruin. We first provide a full characterization of the set of distributions that can be attained before ruin occurs. Then, we formulate two optimization problems that tackle the issue of what to do if the originally specified distribution is either not attainable or not optimal: finding the attainable distribution closest to an unattainable distribution and selecting an optimal attainable distribution under first-order stochastic dominance constraints if the originally specified distribution is attainable, but not optimal. We provide sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of solutions to these constrained convex optimization problems in an extended \(f\)-divergence framework, provide an analytic characterization of the solutions, and present numerical examples.
item.dc:creator: Sixian Jin, Stephan Sturm

item.title: Matching Upper and Lower Bounds for Higher-Order Nonconvex Finite-Sum Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.28202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish tight randomized higher-order oracle complexity for finding first-order stationary points of nonconvex finite sums. Let $n$ be the number of components, $\Delta>0$ the initial objective-gap bound, $L_p>0$ an individual $p$-th derivative Lipschitz bound, and $\epsilon>0$ the target gradient norm. For every fixed integer $p\ge 2$, the minimax number of exact component queries returning the value and all derivatives through order $p$, with success probability at least $2/3$, is \[ \Theta_p\!\left( n+\Delta L_p^{1/p}n^{1-1/(2p)} \epsilon^{-(p+1)/p} \right), \] where the constants depend only on $p$ and the worst case ranges over all finite dimensions. The lower bound holds for unrestricted randomized adaptive algorithms and closes the $\sqrt{n}$ gap between the previously known general-order upper and lower bounds in their dependence on $n$. We extend dense weak hiding to complete higher-order replies while keeping each component's regularity independent of the chain length. The matching upper bound retains the known finite-sum exponent, requires only mean-squared $p$-th derivative increments, and removes the fixed-confidence logarithmic loss by verifying entire recursive-estimation epochs with exact function values. The characterization includes the additive $n$ term for every positive parameter regime; it counts oracle calls with unrestricted internal computation.
item.dc:creator: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.17842v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Birkhoff pseudospectral methods replace the differentiation matrices of classical transcriptions with integration operators whose conditioning does not deteriorate with polynomial order. This paper presents theoretical and computational advancements toward their practical use in aerospace optimal control. The initial-point-anchored Birkhoff integration operator is constructed explicitly for flipped Legendre-Gauss-Radau grids and related exactly to the corresponding Lagrange differentiation matrix and, through a reflection, to the standard Radau Birkhoff operator, whose conditioning properties it inherits. Rate constraints on nonlinear functions of states and controls are enforced directly through the pseudospectral operators and, for control-rate limits, shown to be primal and dual equivalent to state augmentation. Non-affine time mappings concentrate the nodes around localized trajectory features, and composing affine scaling and equilibration transformations provides a systematic way to construct scaling strategies. The methods are implemented in the open-source MATLAB framework RAPTOR and tested across a range of challenging optimal control problems, including a dense-grid orbit-raising problem, a rate-limited landing scenario, a Space Shuttle entry problem, and a five-phase reusable-launch-vehicle mission.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Minnozzi, Marco Sagliano

item.title: Benign Degeneracy for First-Order Methods in Exact Boolean Moment-SOS Relaxations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pseudo-Boolean optimization -- minimizing a polynomial over $\{\pm 1\}^n$ -- includes MAX-CUT, binary quadratic optimization, and Ising models. The moment-sum-of-squares (Moment-SOS) hierarchy provides certified semidefinite relaxations that are often empirically exact at low order. We ask: once a relaxation is exact, how difficult is the resulting semidefinite program (SDP) to solve with first-order methods? Exactness does not imply regularity. At every order $d \ge 2$, a unique rank-one moment optimum is primal degenerate; moreover, if one optimal SOS certificate is strictly complementary, then the certificate set is positive-dimensional and contains singular boundary points. Thus first-order methods may converge to such singular points, around which pointwise analyses that assume regularity at the limit cannot establish a local linear convergence rate. We show that, for exact Boolean Moment-SOS relaxations in their canonical quotient form, this degeneracy is nevertheless benign. We develop an abstract mechanism, which we call residual-field rigidity, that propagates regularity from the relative interior of the optimal set to its singular boundary. It requires neither the primal nor the dual optimal solution to be unique, and it is equivalent to the first-order stall directions of the residual coinciding with the tangent directions of the optimal set. For Boolean Moment-SOS, unique rank-one exactness and the existence of one strictly complementary certificate suffice to trigger this mechanism, yielding a uniform error bound around the entire optimal set. Consequently, ADMM, sGS-ADMM, and PDHG converge eventually linearly from every initialization, even when their limiting certificate is singular. Finally, outside a lower-dimensional semialgebraic exceptional set of Boolean objectives, these hypotheses hold simultaneously at every uniquely rank-one exact order.
item.dc:creator: Shucheng Kang

item.title: Certifiably Correct Fr\'echet Means in Orbit Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24191v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Fr\'echet means in orbit spaces of finite orthogonal group actions. Since computing these means is NP-hard in general, we take inspiration from group synchronization to develop tractable spectral and semidefinite relaxations. Pairwise alignment certifies global optimality and we develop a semidefinite certificate that can extend beyond this condition. For Gaussian data modulo sign, we prove that our certificate succeeds in a high-noise regime where alignment fails. Numerical experiments evaluate these methods in various settings, including summarizing ensembles of districting plans and clustering time series
item.dc:creator: Dustin G. Mixon, Tom Needham, Nathan Willey

item.title: Explicit Steady-State Approximations for Parallel Server Systems with Heterogeneous Servers
item.description: arXiv:2406.04203v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the steady-state performance of parallel-server systems under an immediate routing architecture with two sources of heterogeneity: server types and job classes, often subject to compatibility constraints. We focus on the weighted-workload-task-allocation (WWTA) routing policy, a load-balancing scheme known to be throughput-optimal for such systems. Under a relaxed complete-resource-pooling (CRP) condition, we prove a strong form of state-space collapse in heavy traffic and that the scaled server workloads jointly converge in distribution to a deterministic vector multiplied by an exponential random variable, whose mean is explicitly given by system primitives. Our analysis yields three main insights. First, the conventional heavy-traffic assumption of a unique static allocation plan can be dropped; a relaxed CRP condition suffices. Second, the limiting workload distribution is shown to be independent of the local scheduling policies at the servers, allowing substantial flexibility. Third, the inefficient (non-basic) activities identified by the static allocation problem are proved to receive an asymptotically negligible fraction of routed jobs and service effort, even though WWTA has no prior knowledge of which activities are non-basic, highlighting its robustness to changing arrival rates.
item.dc:creator: Yaosheng Xu

item.title: Jacobian Descent for Multi-Objective Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2406.16232v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many optimization problems require balancing multiple conflicting objectives. To generalize gradient descent, which is limited to single-objective optimization, we introduce Jacobian descent (JD) and its stochastic variants. This algorithm iteratively updates parameters using the Jacobian matrix of a vector-valued objective function, in which each row is the gradient of an individual objective. While several methods to combine gradients already exist in the literature, they generally struggle when the objectives conflict. In contrast, we propose projecting gradients to fully resolve conflict. We prove convergence to the Pareto front in the smooth convex case with this approach, a stronger guarantee than the usual convergence to a weakly Pareto stationary point. Our method also enables instance-wise risk minimization (IWRM), a novel learning paradigm in which the loss of each training example is considered a separate objective. Early experimentation on image classification shows promising results for IWRM. Lastly, we provide an efficient implementation of JD using the Gramian of the Jacobian matrix to drastically reduce memory requirements.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Quinton, Val\'erian Rey

item.title: Optimal Guarantees for Online Selection Over Time
item.description: arXiv:2408.11224v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Prophet inequalities are a cornerstone in optimal stopping and online decision-making. Traditionally, they involve the sequential observation of $n$ non-negative independent random variables and face irrevocable accept-or-reject choices. The goal is to provide policies that provide a good competitive ratio against the optimal offline solution that can access all the values upfront---the so-called prophet value. In the \emph{prophet inequality over time problem} (POT), the decision-maker can commit to an accepted value for $\tau$ units of time, during which no new values can be accepted. This creates a trade-off between the duration of commitment and the opportunity to capture potentially higher future values. In this work, we provide best possible worst-case competitive ratios in the IID setting of POT for single-threshold algorithms and the optimal dynamic programming policy. We show a single-threshold algorithm that achieves a competitive ratio of $(1+e^{-2})/2\approx 0.567$, and we prove that no single-threshold algorithm can surpass this guarantee. With our techniques, we can analyze simple algorithms using $k$ thresholds and show that with $k=3$ it is possible to get a competitive ratio larger than $\approx 0.602$. Then, for each $n$, we prove it is possible to compute the tight worst-case competitive ratio of the optimal dynamic programming policy for instances with $n$ values by solving a convex optimization program. A limit analysis of the first-order optimality conditions yields a nonlinear differential equation showing that the optimal policy's asymptotic worst-case competitive ratio is $\approx 0.609$.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Perez-Salazar, Victor Verdugo

item.title: Accelerating Optimization via Differentiable Stopping Time
item.description: arXiv:2505.22509v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optimization is an important module of modern machine learning applications. Tremendous efforts have been made to accelerate optimization algorithms. A common formulation is achieving a lower loss at a given time. This enables a differentiable framework with respect to the algorithm hyperparameters. In contrast, its dual, minimizing the time to reach a target loss, is believed to be non-differentiable, as the time is not differentiable. As a result, it usually serves as a conceptual framework or is optimized using zeroth-order methods. To address this limitation, we propose a differentiable stopping time and theoretically justify it based on differential equations. An efficient algorithm is designed to backpropagate through it. As a result, the proposed differentiable stopping time enables a new differentiable formulation for accelerating algorithms. We further discuss its applications, such as online hyperparameter tuning and learning to optimize. Our proposed methods show superior performance in comprehensive experiments across various problems, which confirms their effectiveness.
item.dc:creator: Zhonglin Xie, Yiman Fong, Haoran Yuan, Zaiwen Wen

item.title: Gradient Descent on Logistic Regression: Do Large Step-Sizes Work with Data on the Sphere?
item.description: arXiv:2507.11228v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gradient descent on logistic regression has many fascinating properties not fully captured by classical analyses. For linearly separable data, the iterates converge in direction to the maximum-margin separator regardless of how large the step size is. For non-separable data, however, cycles may occur even for step sizes below the local stability threshold of $2/\lambda^*$, where $\lambda^*$ is the largest eigenvalue of the Hessian at the solution. We ask whether requiring all examples to have equal norm is a sufficient condition for global convergence below this threshold. We prove that this is indeed true in one dimension. In higher dimensions, even equal-norm datasets can produce cycles, although global convergence holds for the population loss when the examples are uniformly distributed on the sphere. Finally, in one dimension, we relax the equal-norm assumption to an annulus condition that ensures global convergence below the stability threshold, suggesting a path towards analogous sufficient conditions in higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Si Yi Meng, Baptiste Goujaud, Antonio Orvieto, Christopher De Sa

item.title: Wasserstein Robust Classification Error: Surrogate Loss Misalignment and Distributional Attacks
item.description: arXiv:2510.10000v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (WDRO) provides a framework for evaluating model robustness through the worst-case expectation in the Wasserstein ball around a reference distribution. We prove that ordering hypotheses by increasing WDRO risk is equivalent to ordering them by decreasing robust accuracy if and only if the loss function is a positive multiple of the zero-one loss plus a label-dependent offset. For a class of loss functions including cross-entropy, we show that a hypothesis with perfect robust accuracy can conversely have a higher WDRO risk than another hypothesis with near zero robust accuracy. To evaluate robust accuracy directly, we develop Wasserstein distributional attacks (WDA), which add a weight generation stage after candidate support search to optimize the allocation of empirical mass under the Wasserstein constraint, rather than assigning each data point's full mass to one returned attack point as existing methods do. We further introduce a support-search algorithm for WDA that finds nearby misclassified inputs. On CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, WDA using our search algorithm achieves the lowest adversarial accuracy in most tested settings. Our code is available at https://github.com/OLab-Repo/WDA.
item.dc:creator: Bach C. Le, Tung V. Dao, Binh T. Nguyen, Hong T. M. Chu

item.title: Learning-Based Spectrum Cartography in Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks: A Survey
item.description: arXiv:2605.10359v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks are emerging as important infrastructure for global connectivity and space-based sensing, while their rapidly varying geometry, heterogeneous measurements, and dynamic propagation environments create challenges for acquiring and exploiting spatial radio information. Spectrum cartography provides a framework for constructing and updating spatial representations of radio conditions from sparse observations. This survey reviews learning-based spectrum cartography for LEO satellite networks from an integrated inference--decision perspective. We organize the literature around three representative task categories: radio map reconstruction, localization and state estimation, and map-informed resource allocation. We further examine the progression from classical interpolation, statistical estimation, and structured optimization toward learning-based approaches that exploit environmental context, relational structure, generative modeling, and adaptive information fusion. Particular attention is given to attention mechanisms for learning query- and context-dependent interactions among irregular observations, while distinguishing learned relevance from calibrated measurement reliability. Representative formulations and illustrative examples clarify these modeling principles. Finally, we synthesize cross-cutting lessons and identify open challenges in uncertainty modeling, generalization, dynamic map updating, scalable inference, realistic evaluation, and tighter coupling between radio-map inference and network decision making.
item.dc:creator: Liping Tao, Xindi Tong, Chee Wei Tan

item.title: BERS: Locally Optimal Continuous Algorithm for Maritime Weather Routing with Just-in-Time Arrival
item.description: arXiv:2605.31533v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Maritime weather routing must optimize route geometry under dynamic wind-wave conditions, obstacle constraints, and fixed-arrival requirements. We present B\'ezier Evolve and Refine Strategy (BERS), a two-stage framework that combines global evolutionary search (CMA-ES) with local variational refinement (FMS). Routes are parametrized as B\'ezier curves and evaluated with dense along-path sampling, enabling smooth trajectories while preserving practical feasibility constraints and accounting for mid-segment effects. We evaluate BERS on synthetic benchmarks designed to stress seven operational criteria: continuity, obstacle avoidance, dynamic adaptation, flexible objective design, constant-load feasibility, just-in-time arrival, and local optimality. Across these tests, BERS matches or improves published baselines while maintaining robust convergence under challenging flow fields and land geometries. We then validate the method on real ocean data using hourly ERA5 forcing over 366 daily departures in 2024 for two trans-oceanic corridors (Atlantic and Pacific), with a physics-based model of an 88m cargo vessel with optional rigid wingsails. In real-ocean experiments, route optimization alone reduces mean propulsive energy by 23--59\% versus great-circle baselines of the same propulsion mode. Combined with wind-assisted propulsion, total savings reach up to 75\%. These results show that BERS provides a practical and scalable foundation for just-in-time, energy-efficient weather routing in maritime decarbonization workflows.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Precioso, Francisco Su\'arez, Javier Jim\'enez de la Jara, Rafael Ballester-Ripoll, David G\'omez-Ullate

item.title: Federated learning with heavy-tailed gradient noise and communication noise: a variance-reduction based algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2606.22466v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an emerging distributed machine learning paradigm that enables local devices to jointly train a global model while keeping data decentralized and private. We propose a variance-reduction based algorithm, VRA-FedSGD, for FL in the presence of heavy-tailed gradient noise and communication noise, where these noises are prevalent in large-scale machine learning over wireless networks and Internet of Things deployments. VRA-FedSGD employs a momentum variance reduction technique together with a nonlinear mapping to mitigate heavy-tailed gradient noise, and uses a variance-reduced aggregation mechanism to suppress heavy-tailed communication noise. In the mean sense, VRA-FedSGD achieves a convergence rate of {\small$\mathcal{O}\left(K^{-(p-1)/(2p-1)}\right)$} for nonconvex objective functions, where $p$ is the tail index of heavy-tailed noise. In the almost sure sense, VRA-FedSGD achieves a convergence rate of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(K^{-(1-1/(p-\epsilon))}\right)$ for strongly convex objective functions, where $\epsilon$ is an arbitrarily small constant. Simulated experiments on a logistic regression problem with real-world data verify the effectiveness of VRA-FedSGD.
item.dc:creator: Shengchao Zhao, Yongchao Liu

item.title: Readiness Barrier Functions: Forward-Invariant Control Authority for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation
item.description: arXiv:2608.16335v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Allocation schemes that greedily maximize a readiness metric over the actuator fiber bundle of an overactuated multirotor produce commands that jump between disconnected optimal strata, demanding actuator rates no motor can deliver; effort-minimizing schemes are continuous but cannot guarantee that wrench-rate authority stays above any certified level. We reconcile the two by treating authority as a forward-invariant quantity: a control barrier function on the log-determinant of the drag-aware actuator-authority co-metric, enforced at torque level by a quadratic program in the allocation null space. A single design inequality renders the certified set compact and strictly interior to the actuator box, with the readiness cost of any rotor deactivation given in closed form as $\ln(n/(n{-}m))$ for symmetric designs. An explicit alignment ratio states when tracking can stay exact, otherwise the wrench error is bounded by $\mathcal{O}(\rho^{-1/2})$, and a robust variant handles motor-parameter uncertainty with a closed-form floor shift independent of the airframe matrix. On a hexarotor and a fully-actuated octorotor the closed-form gap matches simulation to machine precision. Over $300$ randomized missions, greedy maximization violates the certified floor in up to $51\%$ of authority-scarce missions, while the proposed filter never leaves the certified set and, in the hardest moment reversal, commits a $79\times$ smaller wrench error. The robust variant holds the floor on all $150$ perturbed plants. A high-fidelity simulation with measured propeller and motor data shows that the floor holds under unmodeled aerodynamics, electrical limits, and delay, and where it stops applying.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Silano

item.title: Sign Propagation of Principal Minors in Fully Semimonotone Matrices and Stone's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.22829v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stone conjectured in 1981 that every fully semimonotone $\mathbf{Q}_0$-matrix is a $\mathbf{P}_0$-matrix; Murthy and Parthasarathy (1995) proved this for orders up to $4$ and for several special classes. We study the principal minors of fully semimonotone matrices $A\in\Ezerof$ without using $\Qzero$. Let $\G(A)$ be the graph whose vertices are the index sets $\alpha$ with $\det A_{\alpha\alpha}\neq 0$ (including $\alpha=\emptyset$), two vertices being adjacent when they differ in exactly one index. We prove that the sign of the principal minor is constant on every connected component of $\G(A)$, and positive on the component of $\emptyset$. Consequences: an $\Ezerof$-matrix with no vanishing principal minor is a $\mathbf{P}$-matrix, and any $\Ezerof$-matrix satisfying a simple ``descending'' condition on its nonvanishing minors is a $\mathbf{P}_0$-matrix. We show that a sign change across two steps through vanishing minors forces strictly positive coupling in the corresponding principal pivotal transform, and that a principal submatrix of minimal order with negative determinant is an almost-$\mathbf{P}_0$ matrix whose inverse lies in $\Ezerof\cap\Nzero$ and has zero diagonal. Explicit examples show that the component structure can contain negative components, that $\det A>0$ does not force $A\in\Pzero$ in $\Ezerof$, that $\Ezerof$ is not invariant under $A\mapsto A+\varepsilon I$, and that $\Ezerof\cap\Pzero$ contains matrices with $\det A>0$ outside $\Qzero$. Stone's conjecture itself remains open.
item.dc:creator: Sajal Ghosh

item.title: The Indefinite Summation Problem for the Laurent Ring
item.description: arXiv:2609.00824v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article solves the Indefinite Summation Problem (ISP) for the difference ring $(A, \alpha)$, where $A$ is the Laurent ring of shift operators on the lattice $\Z^n$, and $\alpha$ is any ring automorphism of $A$ of finite order. The space of summable elements in $(A, \alpha)$ is infinite dimensional, and it is possible to write down an explicit basis for it. The solution translates to a finite procedure involving a matrix multiplication, where the size of the matrix can be estimated. It follows that the arithmetic complexity of the solution can also be determined. These results extend to a solution of the ISP for the ring of functions on $\Z^n$, on which $\alpha$ acts by duality. The article also points out that the solution to the ISP amounts to calculating the group cohomologies $H^i([\alpha], A), i = 0, 1$, where $[\alpha]$ is the cyclic group generated by $\alpha$.

item.title: Shape calculus and automatic differentiation for multi-phase level-set topology optimisation with unfitted finite elements
item.description: arXiv:2609.15084v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present shape calculus techniques and a scalable automatic shape differentiation framework for multi-phase topology optimisation on unfitted discretisations defined by several level-set functions. First we establish general, exact shape calculus expressions in the discrete case for multi-phase systems by leveraging concepts from convex geometry. To complement this theoretical foundation, we introduce an open-source multi-phase automatic shape differentiation framework based on polytopal cutting. This computational framework is validated against both finite differences and our established exact expressions, matching the latter to near machine precision. Furthermore, the proposed automatic shape differentiation is scalable across distributed computing environments, demonstrating near ideal weak scaling up to 1.65 billion finite elements across 13,824 computer cores. We demonstrate our implementation by solving unfitted multi-phase topology optimisation problems for anisotropic diffusion, linear elasticity, and fluid--structure interaction. Together, these theoretical and computational contributions provide a robust and accessible foundation for advancing multi-phase topology optimisation using unfitted finite element methods. In particular, the methods enable the solution of topology optimisation problems involving multi-phase and multi-physics systems with non-trivial boundary conditions. The open-source software is available at https://github.com/zjwegert/GridapTopOpt.jl.

item.title: Global Sobolev Convergence of Howard Iteration for Finite-Horizon Controlled Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2609.15607v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Howard policy iteration for finite-horizon stochastic control problems in which the control enters the diffusion coefficient. Each iteration selects a policy by maximizing the Hamiltonian and evaluates it through a linear parabolic equation. Since the improvement depends on the Hessian, even smooth data can produce discontinuous evaluation coefficients. We prove global convergence in the full parabolic Sobolev space under assumptions that allow this loss of regularity. In one space dimension, bounded measurable coefficients and uniform ellipticity suffice, without a large discount, a short horizon, small diffusion variation, or regularity assumptions on the improving policies. Multidimensional extensions hold under structural conditions on the diffusion matrix. The proof combines monotonicity with a parabolic growth estimate to show that the Bellman residual vanishes in measure. Uniform higher integrability then yields strong convergence of the values, gradients, Hessians, and time derivatives, and constructs the unique strong solution. We also establish residual error bounds, extend the argument to entropy regularization and zero-temperature limits, and obtain quadratic convergence for special one-dimensional models.

item.title: Moment Ambiguity and the Limits of Robust Stochastic Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.31090v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study fundamental information-theoretic limits of robust stochastic optimization when the distribution is known only through its exact moment sequence. We develop a unified framework that produces families of distinct distributions sharing all moments yet inducing radically different optimal decisions, thereby establishing strong impossibility results for a range of decision problems under moment ambiguity. Our binary and $N$-way moment-matching constructions separate quantiles, threshold regions, and online selection opportunities while preserving every moment. For the newsvendor problem, moment equivalence causes quantile ambiguity, inducing any fixed or randomized order quantity to fail arbitrarily badly. For revenue maximization, no deterministic or randomized posted pricing scheme can secure a nontrivial approximation relative to the full-information benchmark. For the secretary problem with cardinal observations, the optimal robust success probability under exact moment disclosure is the classical finite-horizon value $s_m$, even for i.i.d. observations. This value converges to $1/e$, compared with the full-information limit of approximately $0.5801$ due to Gilbert and Mosteller (J. Am. Stat. Assoc., 1966). We also recover and expand upon the recent impossibility result of Correa et al. (STOC, 2026) for prophet inequalities with moment knowledge. For every fixed $r\ge1$, exact moment knowledge can yield at best a $\Theta(1/\log m)$ competitive ratio, even when competing against relaxed benchmarks based on expected $r$-th order statistics or when the algorithm is allowed to select $r$ items.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es Cristi, Matteo Russo, Jiechen Zhang

item.title: An Analytic 0.48-Approximation for Non-Monotone k-Submodular Maximization under a Matroid Constraint
item.description: arXiv:2610.20140v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a randomized polynomial-time $0.48$-approximation for maximizing a nonnegative non-monotone $k$-submodular function under a matroid constraint, for every $k\ge2$. The algorithm combines a top-two label rule with a nested-chain potential and maximum-weight matroid bases. Its analysis reduces the approximation guarantee to a one-dimensional time allocation: a uniform local lower bound leads to a linear differential equation, concavity closes the remaining interval, and two elementary budgets complete the proof. A strict saving in the time budget absorbs sampling and discretization errors, yielding the exact $0.48$ guarantee in the value-oracle model.

item.title: Constrained modularity maximization in complex networks via branch-and-price
item.description: arXiv:2610.26562v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modularity maximization is widely used to identify community structure in complex networks. In many applications, however, community detection must also incorporate prior knowledge and domain-specific requirements beyond network topology. We study constrained modularity maximization with restrictions on the number of communities, must-link and cannot-link relations, and general resource constraints. While fast heuristics can provide high-quality solutions, they generally lack optimality guarantees, whereas exact mathematical-programming approaches can become computationally demanding as the network size and constraint complexity increase. We develop a unified optimization framework offering complementary heuristic and exact solution methods. These include a constrained Louvain heuristic for feasible solution generation, a column-generation heuristic with graph-partitioning-based pricing, and exact branch-and-price algorithms using mixed-integer linear programming and sparse mixed-integer quadratic programming formulations for the pricing subproblem. We develop a cutting-plane procedure providing independent upper bounds to assess solution quality when exact optimization cannot be completed. Experiments on 11 unconstrained networks with up to 1,005 nodes and 30 constrained instances with up to 379 nodes demonstrate the complementary roles of these methods. The column-generation heuristic rapidly improves the constrained Louvain solutions across the tested constraint classes, while branch-and-price using the sparse quadratic formulation solves 29 of the 30 constrained instances to optimality within a one-hour time limit. This formulation becomes particularly effective on larger, sparse, undirected networks by substantially reducing the size of the exact pricing model. Overall, the framework guides method selection to balance computational time, solution quality, and optimality guarantees.
